record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: Find algebraic graph-theoretic characterizations of colored graphs that represent fibered families of PL manifolds, including good torus fibrations, surface bundles, Seifert manifolds, manifolds with torus actions, and circle bundles. The colored graph should represent the manifold through the standard construction associating an n-dimensional polyhedron to an (n+1)-colored regular graph.

artifact.category_tag: Edge-colored graphs and crystallizations of manifolds
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on crystallization theory provides characterizations of colored graphs representing closed PL manifolds and some specific classes (e.g., tetrahedron manifolds, certain branched coverings, lens spaces), but no general algebraic graph-theoretic characterization of colored graphs representing the listed fibered families (good torus fibrations, surface bundles, Seifert manifolds, manifolds with torus actions, circle bundles) appears in the literature. The problem is generally stated as open.

status_evidence.title: Manifold crystallization - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Crystallization theory associates edge-colored graphs to PL manifolds and provides combinatorial criteria for manifold recognition.
status_evidence.claim: General crystallization framework exists but the cited specific characterizations for fibered families are not provided.

status_evidence.title: Tetrahedron manifolds via coloured graphs - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Tetrahedron manifolds are shown to be 2-fold coverings of the 3-sphere branched over suitable links, leading to classification as Seifert fibered spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Only specific sub-families have been characterized via colored graphs, not the full classes listed.
